⚠️ Failure Symptom & Factory Service Manual Root Cause

Symptom on machine: The gas water heater pilot goes out and refuses to relight, or the Honeywell status LED blinks a fault code because the Flammable Vapor Sensor (FVS) mounted near the floor has triggered.

Verified technical root cause: The white plastic Flammable Vapor Sensor (SP20172) clipped to the lower left side of the tank has absorbed moisture, paint fumes, or cat litter dust, permanently shifting its resistance above 45,000 Ohms and locking out the Honeywell gas control valve.

🔧 Step-by-Step DIY Inspection & Replacement Checklist

  1. Count the LED flashes on the front Honeywell gas valve: 7 flashes (or 6-1 flashes) means Flammable Vapor Sensor lockout.
  2. Test resistance across the two pins of the white SP20172 sensor clip at the bottom exterior of the tank: a healthy sensor reads 9,000 to 45,000 Ohms. If it reads over 50k Ohms, plug in the new SP20172 sensor and reset the gas valve.

❓ Frequently Asked Questions (Pilot Won't Stay Lit / 2 or 7 Flashes on Honeywell Gas Valve)

How do I clear the 7-flash lockout on the Honeywell gas valve after plugging in the new SP20172 sensor?
Turn the control knob to OFF, wait 30 seconds, turn it to PILOT, and as soon as the status LED starts blinking rapidly, immediately rotate the temperature dial all the way from LOW to HOT and back to LOW 6 times within 30 seconds.
